anti_overlap: Does not review replay-hash determinism, save-format compatibility, or cross-player federation mechanics — that is the deterministic-simulation/replay-engineering reviewer's domain

Does not review whether the two games are independently playable as a live-service/multiplayer product, era-misreading as player-facing rendered content, or R7 federation sequencing — that is the async-multiplayer/live-service design reviewer's domain

Touches trace possession only from the identity/agency angle (does possession change what autonomy means for that resident); the conflict-resolution/merge-semantics and schema-versioning angle belongs to the replay-engineering reviewer
decision_lens: Score P0 when the bounded-vocabulary / week-tick-only / gate-10-determinism guardrail is asserted but has no enforcement mechanism named (no fixed enum, no cap, no CI check) — meaning it is a wish, not a constraint, and will drift the way Talk of the Town's did. Score P1 when the full-sim commitment (approach B) has no observable payoff before the async join exists, or when a question marked 'deferred' actually determines the resident schema (so deferring it is really deferring a schema decision, not a design decision). Score P2 when a design gap only bites at a later integration point (e.g. possession semantics, vocabulary authorship) but doesn't threaten the current commitment. Score P3 for naming/polish.
focus: Whether the resident-sim's own simulation design — full week-tick autonomy, the bounded habitus vocabulary, and trace-possession-as-identity — is a sound generative-agent architecture or a restated version of the tarpits (Talk of the Town, Dwarf Fortress personality systems) it claims to avoid.
name: fd-simdesign-resident-autonomy
persona: Apply the perspective of a generative agent-based social-simulation architect who has shipped and post-mortemed autonomous-NPC systems in the Talk of the Town / Dwarf Fortress / RimWorld / Smallville-LLM-agents lineage — someone who has personally watched a 'bounded' trait vocabulary become unbounded through relationship-graph combinatorics, and who evaluates every new resident-sim proposal by asking what its week-tick actually computes and what stops that computation from growing.
review_areas: Enforcement mechanism for the 'bounded habitus vocabulary' — is there a named closed set, a numeric cap, or a schema constraint, or is 'bounded' doing rhetorical work with no code-level teeth (the exact way Talk of the Town's trait/relationship space escaped its intended bounds)?

Week-tick-only as a simulation boundary — does it actually prevent day-grain state from leaking back into resident-sim (e.g. via fashionsomething's 'reading' of a resident influencing what gets committed at the next week tick), or is the read/write direction underspecified?

The B-over-A ROI case — name the concrete week-tick outputs (ties, routine, habitus) that are observable and matter to a player or to city-sim BEFORE any join exists; if none exist pre-join, the 'generator is the point' rationale is unfalsifiable at ship time

Possession as an identity/agency question (not a merge-conflict question) — when a trace possesses a seeded resident, does the resident's autonomous week-tick simulation stop, degrade, or continue underneath the possession; does the design's own claim that 'consumers cannot tell Seed from Trace apart' hold if possession changes simulation behavior in a way a careful player could detect

Habitus vocabulary authorship — decision-adjacent open Q1 asks whether fashionsomething's Goffman/Bourdieu stack is the vocabulary's author; evaluate whether a single fast-layer game authoring the vocabulary for a shared slow-layer entity creates a hidden coupling that contradicts the shear-boundary rule (§11) even though it isn't a Cargo dependency

Scope creep vectors specific to autonomous social sim — ward pressures exposure (open Q2), tie-graph growth, and routine complexity are the three classic places generative-agent systems quietly become O(n²) or unauthorable; check whether any of the three has a stated ceiling

severity_examples.condition: No fixed vocabulary list, cap, or automated check is named for habitus attributes, ties, or routine complexity.
severity_examples.scenario: The habitus vocabulary is never bounded by an explicit enum, numeric cap, or CI-checked schema constraint anywhere in the design — 'bounded' is asserted as a guardrail with no mechanism — so week-tick simulation of ties, routine, and (per open Q2) possibly ward-pressure exposure for every resident in every ward can grow exactly the way Talk of the Town's did, and nothing in the design would surface the drift before content authors are hand-debugging thousand-resident trait combinatorics.

severity_examples.condition: No pre-join observable divergence between B's week-tick output and A's casting-registry output is specified or testable.
severity_examples.scenario: Full resident-sim (approach B) is committed before any join-side prototype shows week-tick autonomy producing resident state materially different from what a cheap deterministic casting function (approach A) would produce — if the only externally observable output of the week-tick sim before the join exists is 'who lives where and what's their name,' approach B is paying ongoing simulation cost for approach A's payoff, and the brainstorm names no acceptance test that would catch this before the crate is built.

severity_examples.condition: Possession semantics are listed only under Open Questions with no note that the choice constrains the resident record's shape.
severity_examples.scenario: Trace possession is deferred as 'just' an open question (Q3), but a 'conflict' case — two traces claim the same seeded resident — requires a merge policy that determines whether a resident record carries a possession history, a single current owner, or a queue; deferring the semantics risks a schema migration once the answer lands, and the design doesn't flag that the deferral is schema-shaped rather than behavior-shaped.

source_domain: generative agent-based social simulation (Dwarf Fortress personality systems, Talk of the Town, RimWorld, Smallville-style LLM agent architectures)
success_hints: Vocabulary, tie-graph, and routine complexity each have a named ceiling or closed enum, not just the word 'bounded'
At least one week-tick output is identified that is observable and meaningful before the async join exists, giving approach B a falsifiable pre-join payoff
Possession's effect on ongoing week-tick autonomy (pause vs override vs coexist) is addressed, even provisionally, rather than left fully open
The habitus-vocabulary-authorship question (open Q1) is evaluated against the shear-boundary rule, not just against runtime dependency direction
